extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, grant applicants, institutional research administrators, and grant support staff
extracted.subtask_description: A news roundup of recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource updates intended to inform applicants and awardees about changes (e.g., review processes, data sharing formats, highlighted topics, and new award mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models / New Approach Methodologies (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease; investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions, with a focus on approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential (including NAMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use models that best address the scientific question; consider human relevance and translational potential when choosing or proposing NAMs. NIH encouragement of NAMs does not replace the requirement that the chosen model be scientifically appropriate for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format has been issued based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans for applicable applications, use the new 2026 pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified by NIH. (The news item signals an official change in expected DMS plan structure and content.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability of biomedical research is foundational; NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative encourage embedding replication and reproducibility considerations throughout NIH-supported research, including as a Highlighted Topic for applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address replication and reproducibility explicitly in applications (study design, replication plans, transparency, statistical rigor). Expect emphasis in review and potential funding initiatives incentivizing replication. The initiative aims to institutionalize replication efforts across the enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the 'competitive but not discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review after the lapse in appropriations, NIH designated the middle third of applications in a study section as 'competitive but not discussed' to recognize that strong applications may fall below a 33% cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand that being scored in the middle third may result in a 'competitive but not discussed' label — meaning the application is competitive but will not be discussed at the study section meeting. This affects interpretation of review outcomes and next steps (e.g., resubmission strategy, Just-in-Time actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn PF5 Collaborative International Research Project application features and format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH released a 6-minute video overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure describing key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective PF5 applicants should review the overview to understand application formatting requirements, structural features (e.g., potential splitting into linked awards), and review-related procedural details so proposals are prepared in the expected format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of centralized peer review consolidation and its impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH consolidated all peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) in March 2025; NIH reports initial effects on efficiency, competition, and transparency as part of ongoing changes to peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutional staff should be aware that centralized review may change study section composition, review timelines, and administrative/procedural details. Consider these changes when planning submissions and anticipating review/award timelines.
